I read the test file and the implementation actually present in this repo, `xarray/structure/alignment.py`. The test class has two real test methods that call `reindex_variables` three times total: one masked reindex with `[-1]` present, one unchanged reindex with `[0,1,2]`, and another masked reindex with `[-1]` present.

To answer DU-pair coverage for `new_var`, I used the oracle parser logic as a guide for what counts:
- definitions are `Assign` nodes whose target is `new_var`
- uses are reads of `new_var` on the right-hand side of an assignment

In `reindex_variables`, the only assignments to `new_var` are:
- line 79: `new_var = var._getitem_with_mask(...)`
- line 84: `new_var = var.copy(deep=copy)`
- line 86: `new_var = var[indxr]`

Then I checked for assignments whose value reads `new_var`. There is one such use line:
- line 88: `new_variables[name] = new_var`

So the total DU-pairs are the Cartesian product of 3 def lines × 1 use line = 3 pairs:
- (79, 88)
- (84, 88)
- (86, 88)

Now, from the code and the test inputs:
- When any indexer contains a negative value, line 59 adds the dim to `masked_dims`, line 76 makes `needs_masking` true, and line 79 defines `new_var`. Both masked calls in the tests take this path, so pair (79, 88) is covered.
- When the indexer equals `np.arange(dim_sizes.get(dim, 0))`, line 61 adds the dim to `unchanged_dims`; then line 73 converts that dim’s indexer to `slice(None)`, so `indxr` becomes full slices. At line 80, `all(is_full_slice(k) for k in indxr)` is true, so line 84 defines `new_var`. The unchanged call in the tests takes this path, so pair (84, 88) is covered.
- The remaining definition at line 86 is the `else` branch, reached only when reindexing is needed but not masking, and not all entries in `indxr` are full slices. None of the provided tests use such a non-negative, non-identity fancy indexer, so this pair is not covered.

Therefore not all DU-pairs are covered, with 2 covered out of 3 total.
